If by **“UK development finance”** you mean **property development finance / residential development lending**, the short version is:

- There is **no single official UK series** that cleanly reports the whole “development finance market” in one place, so most market sizing is pieced together from **Bank of England lending data, lender disclosures, and specialist industry datasets**. ([wwwtest.bankofengland.co.uk](https://wwwtest.bankofengland.co.uk/boeapps/database/FromShowColumns.asp?CategId=5&FromCategoryList=Yes&HighlightCatValueDisplay=Real+estate+and+related+activities+on+a+fee+or+contract+basis&NewMeaningId=RF&Travel=NIxAZxI4x&utm_source=openai))
- The broad credit backdrop improved through 2025: the Bank of England reported **£3.4bn net lending to private non-financial corporates in July 2025**, while noting continued monitoring of commercial real estate refinancing conditions. ([bankofengland.co.uk](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/statistics/money-and-credit/2025/july-2025?utm_source=openai))
- In the specialist property-finance segment, industry reporting pointed to stronger activity in 2025: **Brickflow said £1.2bn of searched loan value progressed to approval** across development, bridging and commercial lending. That is useful directional evidence, though it is **platform data rather than whole-market data**. ([propertyreporter.co.uk](https://www.propertyreporter.co.uk/development-and-bridging-finance-surges-in-2025.html?utm_source=openai))
- Government-backed supply also expanded: **Homes England’s National Housing Bank structured finance offer** was launched to support medium and large housing developments with **senior and mezzanine lending**, indicating additional institutional support for development funding. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-housing-bank-structured-finance-for-medium-and-large-housebuilders?utm_source=openai))
- Market conditions remained selective rather than loose: the Bank of England’s 2025 Financial Stability reporting still highlighted **commercial real estate lending exposures** at major UK banks, and its July 2025 stability report said **CRE prices had broadly stabilised but refinancing challenges remained**. ([bankofengland.co.uk](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/financial-stability-report/2025/financial-stability-report-december-2025.pdf?utm_source=openai))

**Practical takeaway:** the UK development finance market in 2025 looked **open but disciplined**—capital was available for better-structured schemes, but lenders were still cautious on leverage, exit risk, and refinancing. That is an inference from the mix of Bank of England stability commentary, lender exposure data, and specialist-market activity reports. ([bankofengland.co.uk](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/financial-stability-report/2025/financial-stability-report-december-2025.pdf?utm_source=openai))

If you want, I can turn this into any of these:

1. **A market-size summary table**  
2. **Top UK development finance lenders and pricing**  
3. **UK development finance rates / LTGDV / LTC benchmarks**  
4. **A 2024–2026 trend note for investors or credit committees**  
5. **Excel-ready data points with sources**  

If you mean a different market by “development finance” — for example **DFIs/development banks** rather than **property development lending** — say that and I’ll reframe it.
